Apple CEO Tim Cook announced today that Apple will donate to support relief efforts following the earthquake in Indonesia. Details below.

Apple to donate in support of Indonesia earthquake relief efforts

Over the past few years, Apple has consistently donated to disaster relief efforts following major earthquakes, floods, and other emergencies around the world.

In just the past two months alone, Apple has provided support for relief efforts in Venezuela, Southern Europe, and Japan. Apple CEO Tim Cook announced today that the company will also donate for disaster relief following the 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck Indonesia over the weekend.

As usual, Cook did not disclose the amount of Apple's donation, nor did he specify which organizations would receive the funds.

9to5Mac's Take

Beyond donating after natural disasters and other emergencies, Apple also runs an internal giving programme called Employee Giving, which through the company's donation matching policy has raised over US$880 million to date.

Since Tim Cook announced his decision to step down as Apple CEO, there has been much discussion about the legacy he leaves behind. Apple's commitment to charitable and humanitarian relief work is an important part of his tenure, and it is hoped this will continue under John Ternus's leadership.
